papers.abstract: Abstract Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron–electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U–C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage for Sensing Properties of Classical Fields
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, Ishaan Kannan
papers.summary_en: This paper introduces quantum signal learning, expanding precision sensing to simultaneously estimate multiple classical signal properties with quantum noise suppression below vacuum fluctuations.
papers.summary: Modern precision experiments often probe unknown classical fields with bosonic sensors in quantum-noise-limited regimes where vacuum fluctuations limit conventional readout. We introduce quantum signal learning, a sensing framework that extends metrology to a broader property-learning setting, and propose a quantum-enhanced protocol that simultaneously estimates many properties of a classical sign
papers.abstract: Modern precision experiments often probe unknown classical fields with bosonic sensors in quantum-noise-limited regimes where vacuum fluctuations limit conventional readout. We introduce quantum signal learning, a sensing framework that extends metrology to a broader property-learning setting, and propose a quantum-enhanced protocol that simultaneously estimates many properties of a classical signal with shot noise suppressed below the vacuum level. Our scheme requires only two-mode squeezing, passive optics, and static homodyne measurements, and enables classical estimation of many properties from the same experimental dataset. We prove that our protocol enables a quantum speedup for common classical sensing tasks, including measuring electromagnetic correlations, real-time feedback control of interferometric cavities, and Fourier-domain matched filtering. To establish these separations, we introduce an optimal-transport conditioning method and show both worst-case exponential separations from all entanglement-free strategies and practical speedups over homodyne and heterodyne baselines. We further show that when squeezing is treated as a resource, a protocol with squeezed light can sense a structured classical background exponentially faster than any coherent classical probe.
papers.physics_advance: Experimental protocol demonstrating quantum speedup in sensing classical field properties beyond vacuum noise limits using bosonic sensors and squeezed light.
papers.relevance_reason: Introduces a quantum sensing framework with experimentally realizable protocols that surpass classical limits, providing new insights into quantum noise-limited bosonic sensing of classical fields.

papers.title: A functional two-pore-domain K + channel from a large DNA virus
papers.authors: Oliver Rauh, Sebastian Mach, Oliver Clarke, Jonas Toews, James L. Van Etten, Mike Althaus, Anna Moroni, Gerhard Thiel

papers.abstract: The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K + channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. K2P channels, which are made from tandem repeats of two pore domains, are not found in prokaryotes and their evolutionary origin is still unknown. In searching for primitive K2P channel precursors, we screened the genomes of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs) for genes coding for K2P channels. This was motivated by two reasons: NCLDVs are already known for coding primitive Kir type channels, and they play important roles in the evolution of eukaryotes. Here, we report that the NCLDV Pyramimonas orientalis virus codes for K2P-like K + channels. With only 178 amino acids and no cytosolic domains, this Kpov protein is much smaller than any eukaryotic K2P channel, but still functional as K + selective channel in lipid bilayers. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kpov is not the product of molecular piracy from the host but may result from fusion of primitive viral K + channel pore domains.

papers.relevance_reason: Discovers a functional viral two-pore K+ channel representative of a simpler evolutionary precursor, revealing insights into ion channel evolution and minimal channel architecture in membranes.

papers.abstract: Molluscan shells come in various shapes and sizes. Despite this diversity, each species produces a shell with a characteristic shape that is independent of environmental conditions. We seek to understand this robust complexity. We are guided by two principles in the spirit of D’Arcy Thompson. First, the growth is governed by the repeated and continuous application of a fixed growth law, even as the shell evolves in overall shape, without any complex biological machinery to monitor and control the growth. Second, the growth law depends solely on local geometry at the shell’s growing edge. The first principle naturally leads to the mathematical statement that the shape of the shell is generated by the action of a Lie group on a protoconch. The second naturally leads to a particular representation of the Lie group. We use this representation to show that the shapes of nearly all known molluscan shells can be described by essentially three parameters: a scalar (scaling), a vector (orientation), and a curve (edge of the protoconch). We relate these parameters to the phylogenetic tree. In addition to the morphogenetic insight, our results potentially point to a alternative growth-based approach to engineering complex structures.

papers.title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d -wave superconductor: A quantum Monte Carlo study
papers.authors: Chuang Chen, Subir Sachdev, Zi Yang Meng
papers.summary_en: This quantum Monte Carlo study evidences a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition between antiferromagnetic insulator and nodal d-wave superconductor at half-filling on a square lattice.
papers.summary: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal d -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. papers.abstract: We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal d -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background π -flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and d -wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the d -wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.
papers.physics_advance: Discovery of a continuous deconfined quantum critical point between Néel antiferromagnetism and nodal d-wave superconductivity in a π-flux SU(2) lattice gauge theory model.
papers.relevance_reason: Provides compelling quantum Monte Carlo evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition between antiferromagnetic insulator and nodal d-wave superconductor, establishing new understanding of correlated electronic phases.

papers.title: Toward Complete Characterization of Topological Insulators and Superconductors: A Systematic Construction of Topological Invariants Based on Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
papers.authors: Seishiro Ono, Ken Shiozaki
papers.summary_en: This study presents a systematic framework for constructing topological invariants across many symmetry classes using the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence, overcoming limitations of symmetry-indicator theory. It completely characterizes K groups in 159 space groups, including superconductors where symmetry indicators fail.

papers.abstract: The past decade has witnessed significant progress in topological materials investigation. Symmetry-indicator theory and topological quantum chemistry provide an efficient scheme to diagnose topological phases from only partial information of wave functions without full knowledge of topological invariants, which has resulted in a recent comprehensive materials search. However, not all topological phases can be captured by this framework, and topological invariants are needed for a more refined diagnosis of topological phases. In this study, we present a systematic framework to construct topological invariants for a large part of symmetry classes, which should be contrasted with the existing invariants discovered through one-by-one approaches. Our method is based on the recently developed Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space. As a demonstration, we construct topological invariants for time-reversal-symmetric spinful superconductors with conventional pairing symmetries of all space groups, for which symmetry indicators are silent. We also validate that the obtained quantities work as topological invariants by computing them for randomly generated symmetric Hamiltonians. Remarkably, the constructed topological invariants completely characterize K groups in 159 space groups. Our topological invariants for normal conducting phases are defined under some gauge conditions. To facilitate efficient numerical simulations, we discuss how to derive gauge-independent topological invariants from the gauge-fixed topological invariants through some examples. Combined with first-principles calculations, our results will help us discover topological materials that could be used in next-generation devices and pave the way for a more comprehensive topological materials database.
papers.physics_advance: New comprehensive framework for constructing topological invariants in crystalline symmetry classes beyond symmetry indicators.
papers.relevance_reason: Develops a systematic method to construct topological invariants for a large range of symmetry classes, overcoming limitations of existing approaches and facilitating discovery of novel topological phases.

papers.method_en: The method employs the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space to systematically derive topological invariants, and validates them by computing for randomly generated symmetric Hamiltonians, including gauge fixing and deriving gauge-independent forms for numerical efficiency.

papers.abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

papers.abstract: We investigated the longitudinal thermal conductivity κ xx and thermal Hall conductivity κ xy in La 2 CuO 4 at temperatures T between 2 and 20 K in magnetic fields H up to 10 T. Within the temperature and field intervals studied, we do not resolve any thermal Hall signal with a conservative upper bound of | κ xy / T | < 1 × 10 − 4 Wm − 1 K − 2 . papers.abstract: The protective capsid encasing the genetic material of HIV can traverse the nuclear pore complex (NPC) intact, despite being far larger than conventional passive cargo. This is attributed to the properties of the capsid surface, which promote partitioning into cohesive assemblies of the disordered proteins that form the NPC’s permeability barrier: phenylalanine-glycine nucleoporins (FG-Nups). The implication, at the mesoscale, is that capsid–NPC interactions are characterized by the interfacial physics of wetting and capillarity. To capture this, we develop a minimal theory that reduces to an interplay between capsid geometry, effective cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic contact angles, and a ratio of interfacial tensions. By combining analytical calculations, sharp- and diffuse-interface numerics, we make several predictions: A geometry-dependent trade-off between penetration depth and the wetting transition; asymmetric capillary forces that generate torques and lead to metastable “stalled” states that are tilted; a topological classification of the possible mechanisms underlying the largest energetic barrier; and spontaneous symmetry breaking of displaced FG-Nups. These behaviors connect capsid shape and orientation to the topology and symmetry of FG-Nup displacement, and to the molecular compositions on each side of the pore. They are consistent with published cryoelectron tomography orientations, which provide an initial estimate of the cytoplasmic contact angle. Crucially, our results identify a capillary advantage for the HIV capsid’s characteristic broken-symmetry geometry.

KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 unit
papers.abstract: Abstract Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted p K a values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based p K a prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

papers.summary_en: The paper validates a one-mode electron correlation approach for calculating correlation energies using stationary Hartree-Fock states with a universal parameter-free source-return construction.

In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before
papers.abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+δ^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

papers.authors: David A. Herrera-Martí, Marc Jamin
papers.summary_en: A phenomenological mean-field model for intrinsically disordered protein condensates is proposed, explaining inverse and reentrant phase transitions as functions of salt concentration through entropic forces arising from integrating out fast-moving molecular species.
papers.summary: We present a phenomenological, mean-field model for condensates of intrinsically disordered proteins that describes inverse phase transitions and qualitatively predicts reentrant phase behavior as a function of salt concentration. The model is based on a matrix-based formulation of the Flory-Huggins free energy, in which the enthalpic interaction parameter and the protein valence, defined here as
papers.abstract: We present a phenomenological, mean-field model for condensates of intrinsically disordered proteins that describes inverse phase transitions and qualitatively predicts reentrant phase behavior as a function of salt concentration. The model is based on a matrix-based formulation of the Flory-Huggins free energy, in which the enthalpic interaction parameter and the protein valence, defined here as the number of effective "sticky patches", are treated as free parameters. Its central insight is that integrating out dynamics of fast-moving molecular species generates an effective entropic force that increases the free-energy barrier to mixing, even within a mean-field description. We account for this by linking Gaussian integration of co-solutes to the Schur complement of the matrix-based Flory-Huggins free energy. This provides a general thermodynamic framework illustrating how enthalpic interactions that increase the number of available microstates necessarily induce effective entropic forces. We demonstrate the expressiveness and predictive power of the model by qualitatively reproducing recent experimental observations on the rabies virus phosphoprotein.

papers.abstract: Collective ordering in correlated electron systems emerges from microscopic dynamics, yet the evolution of observable textures need not admit a closed, memoryless description. We introduce a graph-recurrent neural network (GRNN) framework that learns such emergent dynamics directly from trajectories without specifying microscopic equations of motion. The framework integrates gated recurrent memory with graph message passing: local hidden states encode information beyond the instantaneous observables, while spatial coupling allows this information to propagate between sites. The observable and hidden fields evolve jointly through a shared local rule, providing a scalable representation of dynamics with spatial interactions and temporal memory. We demonstrate this framework on the emergent dynamics of charge-density-wave order in the semiclassical Holstein model, successfully reproducing temporal and spatial correlations and dynamical scaling during domain coarsening. By learning finite-time evolution directly, the GRNN offers a route to efficient, data-driven descriptions of collective dynamics with unresolved microscopic degrees of freedom.

papers.summary_en: This study benchmarks fourteen universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against the AFLOW database, highlighting that disagreement between independent DFT databases sets a fundamental limit on the measurable error of MLIPs. When controlling for reference errors, the best uMLIP matches AFLOW data as closely as the Alexandria database does.

papers.abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) are ranked by their formation-energy error against a DFT database, as if that database were ground truth, but independent DFT databases disagree. We benchmark fourteen uMLIPs on 1.45 million ordered intermetallics against AFLOW, which none trained on, and compare every energy and stability error with that disagreement. For half the structures, AFLOW, Alexandria, and OQMD differ by less than 6-8 meV/atom, but a minority differ by far more, raising the average to 16-30. That disagreement sets a floor on any model's measurable error. Re-referenced, the best uMLIP agrees with AFLOW as closely as Alexandria does, and the next four sit 2-7 meV/atom above the floor. Once broken elemental references are screened, the energy and stability rankings agree almost everywhere. Three apparent model failures shrink or vanish under the right control: poorly correlated shear moduli, thousands of "bad" DFT references, and the leader's inflated lead.
papers.physics_advance: Establishment of intrinsic disagreement limits among DFT databases for intermetallic energies and stabilities, setting fundamental error bounds on universal machine-learned interatomic potentials.
papers.relevance_reason: Quantitatively assesses universal machine-learned interatomic potentials by revealing fundamental DFT reference database disagreement as a floor on accuracy, providing general insights into the limits and reliability of MLIPs across alloys.
papers.summary_zh: 本研究对14种通用机器学习原子间势（uMLIPs）进行了基于145万有序金属间化合物的AFLOW数据库的基准测试，指出不同独立DFT数据库之间的分歧设定了机器学习势可测误差的下限。在排除参考误差后，最优的uMLIP与AFLOW数据的吻合度与Alexandria数据库相当。
papers.method_en: The authors benchmark fourteen uMLIPs using formation-energy errors against the AFLOW database, which none of the potentials were trained on, comparing these errors with the disagreement among independent DFT databases (AFLOW, Alexandria, OQMD). They re-reference energies to correct broken elemental references and evaluate energy and stability rankings accordingly.
papers.method_zh: 作者使用14种uMLIP对未参与训练的AFLOW数据库的形成能误差进行基准测试，将这些误差与独立DFT数据库（AFLOW、Alexandria、OQMD）之间的分歧进行比较，并通过重新校准元素参考，评估能量和稳定性排名。
papers.result_en: They find that for about half the structures, databases agree within 6-8 meV/atom, but a minority differ up to 16-30 meV/atom, setting a floor on ML model errors. After adjusting controls, the best model's agreement with AFLOW rivals Alexandria's, and top models lie 2-7 meV/atom above this floor. Three model failure issues (poor correlation of shear moduli, many bad DFT references, inflated leader lead) are resolved under proper controls.
papers.result_zh: 结果表明约一半结构的数据库数据一致性在6-8 meV/原子内，但少部分结构差异高达16-30 meV/原子，这限定了机器学习模型误差的最低水平。调整控制后，最佳模型与AFLOW的吻合度可与Alexandria媲美，前五模型误差仅高于最低水平2-7 meV/原子。通过恰当控制，三个主要的模型失败问题（剪切模量相关性差、大量坏的DFT参考、领导模型优势被放大）得到解决。
papers.future_en: Future work should focus on refining DFT reference databases to reduce discrepancy floors and extending benchmarking with properly controlled references. Improvements in training data quality and reference consistency are crucial for further advancing uMLIP accuracy.
papers.future_zh: 未来工作应着重完善DFT参考数据库以降低不一致的下限，并利用适当控制的参考数据扩展基准测试。提升训练数据质量与参考一致性对于进一步提高uMLIP准确性至关重要。

papers.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
papers.authors: Arsineh Apelian, Tanay Tak, Xuance Jiang, Tsung-Yin Tsai, James S. Speck, Vojtech Vlcek
papers.summary_en: This study establishes localization contrast, the differing localization of valence and conduction band states due to disorder, as a fundamental factor limiting radiative quantum efficiency in semiconductors, specifically demonstrated in InGaN alloys. It highlights that increasing indium content localizes valence-band states more strongly, reducing radiative recombination while enhancing Auger recombination through disorder-induced momentum-space modifications.
papers.summary: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. papers.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates additional low-$Q$ components and enhances the Auger coupling by more than five orders of magnitude relative to pristine GaN. Thus, we provide a microscopic explanation for the competing trends in radiative and Auger recombination. More broadly, our results establish localization contrast as a mechanism through which disorder can control optical and carrier-carrier interactions in semiconductors.
papers.physics_advance: Establishment of localization contrast as a key factor controlling competing radiative and Auger recombination pathways in semiconductor alloys
papers.relevance_reason: Demonstrates how contrasting localization of valence and conduction band states affects radiative versus Auger recombination in disordered InGaN alloys, providing new microscopic insight into disorder-driven carrier recombination mechanisms
papers.summary_zh: 本研究确立了局域化对比，即由于无序导致价带和导带态局域化程度不同，是限制半导体中辐射量子效率的基本因素，特别在InGaN合金中得到验证。研究表明，随着铟含量增加，价带态局域化增强，导致辐射复合减少，而通过无序引起的动量空间结构改变，奥格复合增强超过五个数量级。
papers.method_en: The authors analyze radiative and non-radiative recombination mechanisms in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys by varying indium content, and use microscopic modeling to correlate localization contrast with optical momentum matrix elements and Auger-Meitner recombination enhancements caused by atomic-scale disorder breaking translational symmetry.
papers.method_zh: 作者通过改变随机In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N合金中的铟含量，分析辐射和非辐射复合机制，并利用微观模型将局域化对比与光学动量矩阵元及因原子尺度无序破坏平移对称性而导致的奥格-迈特纳复合增强联系起来。
papers.result_en: Findings show that increasing In content from 13.5% to 22% progressively localizes the valence-band maximum without similarly localizing the conduction-band minimum, reducing interband optical matrix elements and thus radiative recombination. Concurrently, disorder creates low-Q momentum components that amplify Auger recombination rates by over five orders of magnitude compared to pristine GaN. This dual effect explains the competing trends of radiative and Auger recombination and establishes localization contrast as a key disorder mechanism influencing semiconductor optical properties.
papers.result_zh: 结果表明，将铟含量从13.5%增加到22%导致价带最大态逐渐局域化，而导带最小态无明显局域化，降低了带间光学动量矩阵元，从而减少了辐射复合。同时，无序产生的低动量分量显著增强了奥格复合率，与纯GaN相比提升超过五个数量级。该双重效应解释了辐射和奥格复合相互竞争的趋势，并确立了局域化对比作为影响半导体光学性质的关键无序机制。
papers.future_en: Future work may explore localization contrast effects in different semiconductor materials and device contexts, further investigating how disorder tuning can optimize radiative efficiency and suppress non-radiative losses.
papers.future_zh: 未来工作可在不同半导体材料和器件环境中探讨局域化对比效应，进一步研究调控无序如何优化辐射效率并抑制非辐射损失。

papers.title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
papers.authors: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Joan Elias Miro
papers.summary_en: This work presents a UV-complete model in 2+1 dimensions exhibiting a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase persisting at arbitrarily high temperatures with gapless static modes and algebraic correlations even as temperature diverges.
papers.summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. papers.abstract: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

papers.relevance_reason: The authors present a fully UV-complete model in 2+1D showing an unusual Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless ordered phase persisting to arbitrarily high temperature, challenging the conventional understanding of phase transitions in low dimens
papers.summary_zh: 本工作提出了一个2+1维的UV完备模型，展现了贝里辛斯基-科斯特利茨-托勒斯（BKT）有序相，可在任意高温下持续存在，且温度趋于无穷时仍具无隙静态模和代数衰减相关。
papers.method_en: A controlled perturbative construction separates scales leading to a 2D Euclidean effective field theory remaining perturbatively tractable when its soft modes become strongly coupled; the BKT phase boundary is determined via matching to lattice Monte Carlo results.
papers.method_zh: 通过受控微扰构造分离尺度，导出在软模式强耦合时仍可控的二维欧几里得有效场论；BKT相边界通过与晶格蒙特卡罗结果匹配确定。
papers.result_en: The model supports a BKT phase boundary confirmed quantitatively and exhibits a high-temperature phase with gapless static modes and algebraic decay, challenging conventional expectations about BKT transitions.
papers.result_zh: 该模型支持定量确认的BKT相边界，且展现高温相中无隙静态模和代数衰减，挑战了对BKT转变的传统认知。
papers.future_en: Further exploration could include dynamics near the BKT boundary and applications to materials or systems manifesting reentrant high-temperature superfluidity.

papers.title: $π$-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model
papers.authors: Zhaochen Liu, Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale
papers.summary_en: This paper compares two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models—zero-flux and staggered π-flux—at half filling, showing that different charge fluctuation profiles lead to distinct quantum paramagnetic regimes.
papers.summary: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered $π$-flux model with zero and $π$ flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a
papers.abstract: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered $π$-flux model with zero and $π$ flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations, we find that the positive ring-exchange of the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality, consistent with its notion of a chiral spin liquid at intermediate coupling. In the staggered-$π$-flux model, whose noninteracting limit is a Dirac semimetal, the ring exchange changes sign and disfavors chiral order and we find no resolvable scalar chirality. This renders flux-tuned ring-exchange an efficient discriminator between chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnets at finite coupling.
papers.physics_advance: Identification of flux-tuned ring-exchange as a control parameter distinguishing chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnetic regimes in triangular-lattice Hubbard models
papers.relevance_reason: It experimentally and computationally shows how staggered π-flux modifies ring-exchange interactions affecting quantum paramagnetism and chiral order in Hubbard models, offering a new mechanism to control competing spin liquid states.
papers.summary_zh: 本文比较了两种时反对称的三角晶格哈伯德模型——零通量和交错π通量——在半填充时的行为，表明不同的电荷涨落特征导致不同的量子顺磁体区域。
papers.method_en: The authors combine strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations to analyze ring-exchange effects in both models.
papers.method_zh: 作者结合强耦合展开与无限维度矩阵重整化群（iDMRG）计算，分析两种模型中的环交换效应。
papers.result_en: Positive ring-exchange in the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality consistent with a chiral spin liquid, while in the staggered-π-flux model the ring exchange changes sign, disfavoring chiral order and showing no resolvable scalar chirality.
papers.result_zh: 零通量模型中正环交换促进自发手性，与手性自旋液体一致；而在交错π通量模型中，环交换改变量符号，抑制手性序且未观察到标量手性。
papers.future_en: The results suggest that tuning flux can efficiently discriminate chiral versus non-chiral quantum paramagnets, encouraging further studies on flux effects in frustrated systems.

papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic resonance in a bulk $α$-MnTe crystal is investigated using both frequency-domain and time-domain THz spectroscopy techniques. At low temperatures, an excitation at the photon energy of $(3.5\pm 0.1)$~meV is observed and identified as a magnon mode through its distinctive dependence on temperature and magnetic field. This behavior is reproduced using a simplified model for antiferromagnetic resonance in an easy-plane antiferromagnet. The results of our experiments, when compared to exchange constants established in the literature, allow us to extract the out-of-plane component of the single-ion magnetic anisotropy reaching $(40\pm10)$~$μ$eV.

papers.title: Anyon Chern bands of opposite sign and reversed drift
papers.authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Minxuan Wang, Shinsei Ryu
papers.summary_en: This paper studies the dispersion and dynamics of Laughlin quasiholes in a fractional quantum Hall environment under a periodically modulated magnetic field, revealing that modulation splits the quasihole band into subbands with opposite Chern numbers and induces reversed drift directions.
papers.summary: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. papers.abstract: The elementary charged excitations of fractional quantum Hall states are anyons. Without continuous translation symmetry, they acquire a dispersion and richer dynamics. We study the Laughlin quasihole at filling $1/3$ in a periodically modulated magnetic field, a common model of fractional Chern insulators in two-dimensional materials. From the microscopic wave functions, we derive the commutator of its guiding-center coordinates, set by a many-body Berry curvature that governs its wave packets. A modulation with two flux quanta per unit cell splits the quasihole band into bands with Chern numbers $6$ and $-3$; such opposite signs are generic as long as a weak modulation opens a gap between the anyon bands. In the $C=-3$ band, the quasihole drifts against $\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}$, although the magnetic field has the same sign everywhere. Perturbation theory in the modulation explains these results, and large-scale Monte Carlo calculations confirm them. Anyon bands thus acquire their own topology, which controls anyon motion and may shape the phases of itinerant anyons.

papers.authors: Miguel A. Vazquez-Mozo
papers.summary_en: This paper studies anomalous transport in equilibrium fermionic fluids chirally coupled to Weyl-type nonmetricity, identifying chiral separation effects influenced by fluid vorticity and Weyl magnetic fields.

papers.abstract: Anomalous transport in equilibrium fermionic fluids chirally coupled to background Weyl-type nonmetricity is studied. A formal descent analysis is carried out in which the dependence of the anomaly polynomial on the nonmetricity tensor is encoded in a Weyl invariant four-form. The constitutive relation of the axial-vector current is evaluated from the equilibrium partition function obtained using transgression techniques, showing the existence of nonmetricity-mediated chiral separation effects driven by the fluid's vorticity and the Weyl magnetic field. A second nonminimal coupling of fermionic matter to metric-affine geometries proposed in the literature is also discussed.

papers.title: Dipole-exchange spin waves and mode hybridization in magnetic nanoparticles
papers.authors: Fedor Shuklin, Khristina Albitskaya, Sergei Solovyov, Alexander Chernov, Mihail Petrov
papers.summary_en: The paper investigates spin-wave modes and hybridization in confined ferromagnetic resonators with spherical and cylindrical geometry, analyzing the effects of exchange and dipolar interactions.
papers.summary: We investigate spin-wave modes in confined ferromagnetic resonators with spherical and cylindrical geometries across the exchange-dominated, dipole-exchange, and dipolar interaction regimes. Starting from the linearized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, we show that the projection of the total angular momentum and mirror parity are conserved quantities in the problem of axially symmetric resonator
papers.abstract: We investigate spin-wave modes in confined ferromagnetic resonators with spherical and cylindrical geometries across the exchange-dominated, dipole-exchange, and dipolar interaction regimes. Starting from the linearized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, we show that the projection of the total angular momentum and mirror parity are conserved quantities in the problem of axially symmetric resonators. These symmetries provide a natural classification of spin-wave modes and explain the degeneracy of exchange modes, as well as its lifting by dipolar interactions. Numerical analysis shows that the nonlocal dipolar interaction removes the exchange degeneracy and hybridizes modes, leading to avoided crossings between modes that belong to the same symmetry sector. To describe this behavior, we develop a coupled-mode theory formulated directly in terms of dynamical magnetization, which reduces the dipole-exchange problem to a finite system of interacting modes. The resulting framework provides a unified description of spin-wave spectra in confined magnetic particles from the exchange limit to the dipolar regime.

papers.abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting (NRSS) in collinear antiferromagnets, including altermagnets and compensated ferrimagnets, offers a route to high-frequency spintronics immune to stray fields, but its dynamic control has remained elusive. We demonstrate, using density functional theory (DFT) and nonlinear phononics, that THz laser pulses can achieve ultrafast, reversible control of NRSS on picosecond timescales in antiferromagnets. We derive two mode-selection criteria, accounting for phonon and magnetic wavevector compatibility and inversion parity, to identify which phonon modes can activate NRSS. Our calculations illustrate the creation of NRSS in spin-degenerate NiO and the enhancement of existing splitting in LaFeO$_3$. While practical implementation depends on excitation conditions, lattice dynamics, and mode coupling, these results establish design principles for identifying materials with stronger and more accessible responses. Limitations imposed by driving fields, phonon damping, and anharmonic detuning motivate further materials screening based on accessible excitation strengths, lattice stability, resonance frequency matching, and favorable anharmonic coupling.

papers.summary_en: This work explores a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures in spin chains, connecting fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. Using the spin-1 XXC chain as an example, it demonstrates how local deformations reduce fragmentation to a single scar tower, linking several scar models.

papers.abstract: We investigate a hierarchy of invariant Hilbert-space structures connecting Hilbert-space fragmentation, partial solvability, and quantum many-body scars. For spin chains with fragmented spin-$1/2$ subspaces and their local deformations, we show, using the spin-$1$ $XXC$ chain as a representative example, how successive local deformations reduce extensive irreducible-string fragmentation through an implicitly embedded spin-$1/2$ invariant space and ultimately to a single scar tower, connecting the $XXC$, perturbed $XXC$, and spin-$1$ $XY$ scar models. Through the intermediate embedded space, local dynamics couples states from distinct frozen irreducible-string sectors and selects a new decomposition into representations, from which smaller invariant spaces can be retained. We also establish a rigidity constraint on isolating nonsymmetric towers and a constructive correspondence that transfers a reduction between locally realizable representations of the embedded dynamics. The latter demonstrates that the reduction hierarchy can be transferred through a unitary transformation within the embedded subspace, yielding an exact scar tower built on a Néel reference state without requiring unitary equivalence of the full Hamiltonians.

papers.title: Kondo screening and random-singlet formation in highly disordered systems
papers.authors: Lucas G. Rabelo, Igor C. Almeida, Eduardo Miranda, Vladimir Dobrosavljević, Eric C. Andrade
papers.summary_en: A minimal effective framework is presented to capture anomalous low-temperature thermodynamics in strongly disordered systems near metal-insulator transitions by modeling competition between Kondo screening and random-singlet formation.
papers.summary: We introduce a minimal effective framework designed to address the anomalous low-temperature thermodynamics observed in strongly disordered interacting systems near a metal-insulator transition, such as doped semiconductors. Our approach examines how a strongly inhomogeneous electronic bath quenches dilute pairs of local magnetic moments. By solving the resulting two-impurity Kondo-Heisenberg prob
papers.abstract: We introduce a minimal effective framework designed to address the anomalous low-temperature thermodynamics observed in strongly disordered interacting systems near a metal-insulator transition, such as doped semiconductors. Our approach examines how a strongly inhomogeneous electronic bath quenches dilute pairs of local magnetic moments. By solving the resulting two-impurity Kondo-Heisenberg problem within a large-$\mathcal{N}$ variational framework, we capture the competition between Kondo screening and random-singlet formation. Both mechanisms give rise to singular thermodynamic responses, producing a magnetic susceptibility of the form $χ(T)\sim T^{-α}$, where the exponent $α$ evolves smoothly with model parameters and saturates in the metallic regime, consistent with experimental observations. Our results establish a unified framework that connects random-singlet physics and disorder-induced Kondo screening in strongly disordered correlated materials.

papers.authors: Ajay Kumar, Clemens Ulrich, Rajendra S. Dhaka

Phonon anomalies occur around 60 K and 160–180 K, above the Neel temperature, linked to lattice dynamics and local structure.

Interestingly, pronounced changes in the phonon frequencies, linewidths, and intensities are observed around 60~K, well above the long-range antiferromagnetic ordering temperature, $T_{\rm N} \appro
papers.abstract: We report a detailed temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy and Co $K$-edge extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) study of the insulating antiferromagnetic double perovskite SrLaCoNbO$_6$. Interestingly, pronounced changes in the phonon frequencies, linewidths, and intensities are observed around 60~K, well above the long-range antiferromagnetic ordering temperature, $T_{\rm N} \approx 15$~K. These anomalies indicate a modification of the lattice dynamics that may involve local structural distortions, short-range magnetic correlations, or an interplay between them. Additional changes in both high- and low-energy Raman modes are detected near 160--180~K via variations in phonon intensities and linewidths, together with changes in the Fano asymmetry of selected low-energy modes. The asymmetric line shapes of these modes are well described phenomenologically by Fano profiles and indicate coupling of the discrete phonons to an underlying continuum, whose possible microscopic origins are discussed. Moreover, the EXAFS analysis reveals correlated changes in bond distances and Debye--Waller factors around the Co ions near 60~K and 160~K, indicating subtle local structural distortions at temperatures corresponding to the Raman anomalies. The combined Raman and EXAFS results therefore demonstrate a close correlation between anomalous lattice dynamics and local structural evolution in SrLaCoNbO$_6$.

papers.authors: Luigi Camerano, Federico Bisti, Gianni Profeta
papers.summary_en: Using first-principles calculations and Wannier Hamiltonians, the authors identify ligand-mediated hybridization as the dominant microscopic mechanism of altermagnetic spin splitting in Co$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$, rather than direct magnetic-ion hopping.

papers.abstract: Altermagnets host spin-split electronic bands despite zero net magnetization, opening new routes for spintronics beyond conventional ferromagnets. Going beyond symmetry-based classifications, which specify allowed terms but not their hierarchy, here we use first-principles calculations and Wannier Hamiltonian engineering to uncover the microscopic bonding contributions of altermagnetic spin splitting in the $g$-wave altermagnet Co$_{1/4}$NbSe$_2$. We show that the splitting is captured by a short-range tight-binding model, establishing its local origin. By selectively controlling hopping channels, we demonstrate that the dominant contribution arises not from direct magnetic-ion hopping, but from ligand-mediated hybridization that transfers anisotropy to itinerant states. This identifies ligand-assisted coupling as the key mechanism of altermagnetic spin splitting and provides a microscopic bridge between minimal models and symmetry guided first-principles material searches, enabling real-space design of altermagnetic functionality.

papers.authors: Dean Carmi, Riccardo Ciccone
papers.summary_en: This work studies Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ with large $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, deriving bulk propagators and phase diagrams exactly in coupling and level ratios. The authors extract large-$N$ BCFT data for critical and tricritical scalar theories and related fermionic models at bulk conformal points.

First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$
papers.abstract: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $α$ and $κ$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.
papers.physics_advance: Exact determination of spin-one spectra and BCFT data in large-N Maxwell-Chern-Simons theories coupled to matter in AdS$_3$.
papers.relevance_reason: The work provides an exact large-N analysis of Maxwell-Chern-Simons theories coupled to matter in AdS$_3$, identifying bulk photon spectra and boundary conformal data that deepen understanding of gauge-matter interplay and BCFT data extract
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究了AdS$_3$上的Maxwell-Chern-Simons理论，耦合大$N$复标量或狄拉克费米子，准确导出传播子和相图。作者在大$N$极限和共形点提取了关键和三临界标量以及相关费米子模型的边界共形场论数据。
papers.method_en: The authors derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator with Dirichlet boundary conditions clarifying massive and flat sector contributions, and resum matter insertions at large $N$, holding the Chern-Simons level to flavor ratio and gauge coupling scaled quantities fixed. Analytical resummation yields the photon propagator poles characterizing boundary spin-one spectra split by helicities.
papers.method_zh: 作者在Dirichlet边界条件下推导了Maxwell-Chern-Simons传播子，区分了质量和零模贡献；在大$N$极限下对物质插入进行重求和，并固定Chern-Simons水平与味数比以及耦合常数，得到光子传播子的极点表达，刻画由手性分裂的边界自旋一谱。
papers.result_en: They obtain phase diagrams showing phases with protected chiral currents for scalars and helicity-dependent currents for fermions, analyze lifting of symmetry upon Higgsing, and determine large-$N$ BCFT data at conformal points, encompassing critical, tricritical scalar, regular fermion, and Gross-Neveu models. The results clarify the interplay between gauge fields and matter in AdS$_3$ holography.

papers.summary_en: This study uses Mn-deficient and near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals with composition gradients to systematically investigate composition-dependent phase transitions and magnetic properties, revealing abrupt transformation disappearance for Mn below ~22 at.% and associated magnetic behavior.

papers.abstract: Composition gradients formed during directional solidification are generally considered undesirable in Ni-Mn-Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys. However, these gradients offer a highly effective platform for systematically investigating composition-property relationships under identical growth and heat-treatment conditions. To exploit this approach, one Mn-deficient and two near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals were grown by optical zone remelting and characterized by X-ray fluorescence mapping, optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, low-field magnetic measurements, and vibrating-sample magnetometry. The ingots contained elongated grains and axial compositional gradients, primarily associated with the redistribution of Mn and Ga, whereas Ni remained relatively uniformly distributed. The martensitic and premartensitic transformation temperatures generally increased with increasing Mn content. Neither transformation was detected between 10 and 400 K in specimens containing 20.5-22.0 at.% Mn, all of which had $e/a < 7.40$. In contrast, both transformations were observed in the investigated specimens containing at least 22.1 at.% ($e/a \geq 7.46$). This abrupt change may indicate a possible electron-concentration threshold for the occurrence of these transformations. Saturation magnetization increased with Mn content up to 25.8 at.%, reaching 96.9 A m$^2$/kg at 10 K and 71.2 A m$^2$/kg at 300 K. Post-growth annealing increased the transition temperatures and changed the low-field magnetic response. The results indicate that composition-gradient oligocrystals serve as an effective platform for investigating the relationships between composition, structure, and magnetic properties in Ni-Mn-Ga alloys with the same processing history.

papers.title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
papers.authors: Andreas Feuerpfeil, Ronny Thomale, Trithep Devakul, Nicolas Regnault, Julian May-Mann
papers.summary_en: This paper numerically demonstrates an interaction-driven transition from fermionic to bosonic edge phases in double quantum spin Hall insulators, confirming the existence of gapped single-fermion excitations and gapless fermion pairs.
papers.summary: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the
papers.abstract: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and $S^z$ conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe$_2$ and MoTe$_2$. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.

papers.title: Nonlinear Canonical Transformations for Studying Spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Swarnamoy Ghosh, Thomas M. Henderson, Gustavo E. Scuseria
papers.summary_en: This work introduces a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation that maps strongly correlated spin-1/2 Hamiltonians into new spin Hamiltonians more amenable to mean-field treatment, demonstrated on XXZ and J1-J2 models. The approach improves energy accuracy and offers a many-body preconditioning strategy for coupled-cluster approximations in frustrated spin lattices.
papers.summary: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ
papers.abstract: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories are promising, they are not yet black-box methods and require system-specific development. The XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ spin models provide demanding benchmarks. Spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. We introduce a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian into a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and $J_1$-$J_2$ Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions, as nonlocal strings can appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.
papers.physics_advance: Exact nonlinear operator transformation that serves as a many-body preconditioner, improving mean-field and coupled cluster approximations for strongly correlated spin Hamiltonians.
papers.relevance_reason: Proposes a nonlinear spin-fermion-spin transformation that recasts strongly correlated spin Hamiltonians into forms more amenable to mean-field descriptions, enabling improved many-body approximations in strongly correlated spin systems.

papers.title: Nonlinear and Chaotic Dynamics of Two Dipolar-Coupled Anisotropic Spins under Periodic Excitation
papers.authors: Manish Anand
papers.summary_en: The work explores nonlinear magnetization dynamics and chaotic behavior of two dipolar-coupled anisotropic spins under periodic transverse excitation.
papers.summary: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we
papers.abstract: We investigate the non-linear magnetization dynamics of two identical anisotropic macrospins coupled by dipolar interaction and subjected to periodic transverse excitation. The coupled Landau- Lifshitz-Gilbert equations are solved numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method. By combining bifurcation diagrams, local-maxima analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-dimensional stability maps, we characterize how dipolar coupling, transverse driving amplitudes, and uniaxial anisotropy govern the long-time dynamics. The results reveal a non-monotonic reorganization of dynamical regimes, with alternating intervals of enhanced and suppressed instability. Analysis of symmetric and antisymmetric coordinates distinguishes the collective and relative spin responses, while Fourier spectra and three-dimensional trajectories provide complementary frequency-domain and geometrical characterizations. Simultaneous positivity of the two largest Lyapunov exponents identifies parameter regions consistent with hyperchaotic dynamics. Finally, analytical linearization and ferromagnetic-resonance calculations reveal the distinct coupling dependence of the collectivemode frequencies and clarify the limitations of the linearized description beyond the stability thresholds of the collinear reference state. These findings establish a unified framework for understanding the interplay of dipolar coupling, anisotropy, and periodic excitation in the non-linear dynamics of a minimal interacting-spin system.

papers.abstract: We consider interfaces between critical spin-chains in different universality classes, described in the continuum limit by defect/interface conformal field theory (DCFT/ICFT). We focus on a conformal interface between the Tricritical Ising (TIM) and the Ising CFT exploring the possibility of its experimental realizations in the context of Rydberg atom arrays. Our analysis emphasizes non-invertible symmetries and consistency under modular transformations, and uses defect couplings and the defect spectrum -- including in the case of mixed boundary conditions -- to make sharp experimental predictions. The structure of the observables hinges on a newly discovered pattern of emergent ${W}_3$ chiral symmetry for the Tricritical-Ising/Ising interface.

papers.title: Orbital-coherence memory in electrical transport and its self-consistent Maxwell response
papers.authors: Pengfei Zhu
papers.summary_en: The authors develop a reduced framework distinguishing the feedback effects of internal electronic coherence on electrical transport and its self-consistent coupling to Maxwell equations.
papers.summary: An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current. We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force. Under an explicitly stated moment closure and collis
papers.abstract: An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current. We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force. Under an explicitly stated moment closure and collision ansatz, it yields a passive three-state response with an exponentially damped oscillatory memory. The resulting conductivity redistributes a fixed optical weight and predicts a nonmonotonic dependence of dc conduction on coherence damping at fixed remaining parameters. The orbital reduction constrains the coupling and internal frequency through a shared bare splitting, providing a test beyond unconstrained spectral fitting. A charge-conserving spatial extension couples to Maxwell equations through a positive energy balance and separates the constitutive response from longitudinal collective and transverse electromagnetic modes. We formulate complex-conductivity and transmission tests, including the limits of parameter identification over a finite bandwidth. The model supplies a conditional connection between orbital dynamics, transport memory, and electromagnetic observables; conductivity alone does not establish a uniquely quantum mechanism, and a material-specific collision calculation and closure-error assessment remain necessary.

papers.title: Quantum geometry and quantum capacitance in the orbital magneto-electric effect
papers.authors: James H. Cullen, Daniel P. Arovas, Roberto Raimondi, Dimitrie Culcer
papers.summary_en: This paper develops a density-matrix formulation of the orbital magneto-electric effect (OME) in Bloch electrons, revealing intra-band and inter-band contributions with distinct quantum geometric origins and a band-diagonal charge dipole governed by the quantum metric.
papers.summary: The orbital magneto-electric effect (OME), the generation of a steady-state orbital angular momentum (OAM) density by an electric field, is a central component of orbitronics. Nevertheless its microscopic interpretation is complicated by the existence of two qualitatively different contributions: the intra-band Edelstein term stemming from the combined effect of the equilibrium OAM and Fermi surfa
papers.abstract: The orbital magneto-electric effect (OME), the generation of a steady-state orbital angular momentum (OAM) density by an electric field, is a central component of orbitronics. Nevertheless its microscopic interpretation is complicated by the existence of two qualitatively different contributions: the intra-band Edelstein term stemming from the combined effect of the equilibrium OAM and Fermi surface shift, and the inter-band contribution, stemming from Zitterbewegung induced by the electric field. Here we develop a pedagogical density-matrix formulation of the OME within the framework of the modern theory of Bloch-electron OAM, in which the two contributions naturally emerge from distinct parts of the density matrix, and their distinct quantum geometric structures are clearly seen. In the inter-band contribution, in addition to the local- and itinerant-circulation terms, we show that a band-diagonal displacement, or charge dipole, is present, which is linear in the electric field and governed by the normalized quantum metric. For a tilted massive Dirac cone the Zitterbewegung OME and the Fermi-surface orbital response occur for orthogonal electric-field orientations, providing a route to separate them experimentally. The itinerant-circulation contribution is identical to the dipolar one, so in a two-band model the dipole accounts for exactly half of the inter-band response, both in the doped regime and in the insulating gap. Our recent insights identify quantum-metric engineering as a route for enhancing orbital magneto-electric responses and clarify the relation between modern orbital magnetization, polarization, and orbital torque phenomenology.

We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$ ξ''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approa
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed $p$-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$ ξ''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path $({\boldsymbol y}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ from the SL process. For large $T$, ${\boldsymbol y}_T/T$ is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case. We provide evidence that the condition $ξ''(s) < (1-s)^{-2}$ is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure $p$-spin glasses it is within an absolute ($p$-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in $p$. A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.

papers.abstract: Metallo-DNA nanowires serve as a versatile, programmable scaffold for molecular-scale electronics. In this work, we demonstrate that periodic heavy-metal coordination fundamentally reshapes the electronic landscape of DNA, generating dispersive, metal-centered conduction bands rather than isolated localized states. Driven by enhanced inter-layer coupling, where second nearest-neighbor hopping plays a crucial role: the conduction bandwidth can approach 1 eV, more than double that of canonical DNA. These broad bands suggest enhanced robustness of transport against structural fluctuations. As a result of relativistic effects, in these quasi-one-dimensional materials, spin-orbit (SO) coupling enhances band dispersion and governs spin-dependent transport. We predict that although ligand hybridization reduces atomic SO splitting, the effective SO splitting in these nanowires is comparable to the next-nearest-neighbor hopping strength, which results in considerable spin mixing. We find that Hg2+-coordinated nanowire exhibit pronounced spin-flip conductance comparable to spin-conserving conductance across the LUMO manifold. This efficient spin conversion remains robust over extended molecular lengths and is accompanied by a set of highly delocalized unoccupied states with oscillating nodal structures, readily accessible under low-bias transport measurements. In contrast, the Ag+-coordinated nanowires exhibit weak spin-flip scattering that is more than an order of magnitude smaller than spin-preserving transport. This duality establishes the choice of coordination metal as a decisive parameter to govern metal-metal interaction, electron delocalization, and spin-dependent transport. Overall, our findings demonstrate how relativistic effects and quantum confinement intersect in these bio-templated, quasi-one-dimensional molecular conductors.

papers.abstract: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin-1/2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU($N$) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU($N$) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic $^{87}$Sr. Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the 10 spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin-9/2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish $^{87}$Sr quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard model, and provide a new detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.

papers.abstract: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench.For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

papers.abstract: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. This dynamical skyrmion lattice naturally leads to experimentally measurable consequences. In particular, we identify new collective excitations corresponding to chiral shape deformations of the skyrmions, and propose a new positively charged quasiparticle, the skyrmion vacancy. These results establish a qualitatively new form of moiré Chern physics in rhombohedral graphene: an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice whose skyrmions are dynamical low-energy degrees of freedom.

papers.abstract: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

papers.abstract: Moiré superlattices of transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) host strongly interacting Bose-Fermi mixtures in which bosonic excitons coexist with correlated electron lattices. Using ultrafast, time- and energy-resolved photoluminescence (PL) microscopy, we show that strong exciton-electron and exciton-exciton repulsion can enable ballistic exciton transport in a WSe$_2$/WS$_2$ heterobilayer. This ballistic transport is energy selective: repulsive interactions populate higher-energy moiré exciton bands, including the doubly occupied exciton state XX and the exciton-electron co-localized state Xe, exhibiting mean-squared displacement (MSD) with a quadratic time dependence, MSD $\propto t^2$. Transport in the Xe band is jointly governed by exciton and electron correlations. Exciton correlations suppress relaxation into the lower-energy localized exciton state, while generalized Wigner-crystal (GWC) order at fractional electron fillings enhances Auger recombination and the group velocity of the ballistic expansion. A two-dimensional Bose-Fermi Hubbard model solved using time-dependent mean-field methods qualitatively reproduces the measured exciton transport and time-dependent response. It further confirms that strong cross-species interactions allow the electron crystal to perforate the exciton Mott background, enhancing exciton motion. Our results establish moiré TMDs as highly tunable platforms for realizing strongly interacting Bose-Fermi mixtures.

papers.authors: Jack G. Nedell, Craig J. Fennie
papers.summary_en: This first-principles study classifies and analyzes eight structural domain wall classes in low-temperature rhombohedral R3c NaNbO3, identifying a low-energy 109° domain wall compatible with known crystal twinning and proposing a mechanism for the R3c-Pbcm phase transition.

Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and c
papers.abstract: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral $R3c$ phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO$_3$. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109° domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO$_3$. Finally, we find that this class of 109° walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the $R3c$ phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the $R3c \leftrightarrow Pbcm$ phase transition.
